title: george lombard jr hits yankees first 26 grand slam win over rockies  flm 2026 09 10
text:
September 10 - Rookie George Lombard Jr.'s third-inning grand slam was more than enough for the host New York Yankees to pull out a 6-1 victory over the ​Colorado Rockies on Wednesday night.
New York (83-62) won for the 15th time ‌in 22 games thanks to Lombard's first career grand slam, which gave the Yankees a 5-0 lead.
The Yankees loaded the bases, all with two outs, on a single by ​Aaron Judge, a double by Luis Garcia Jr. and a walk ​to rookie Spencer Jones. Lombard hit his third career homer in ⁠28 games since making his major league debut last month when he ​sent a 1-0 slider from Colorado starter Tomoyuki Sugano (12-9) into the right field ​seats.
At 21 years, 99 days, Lombard became the second-youngest Yankee to hit a grand slam. Only Mickey Mantle was younger when he did so twice in a four-day span in ​July 1952 at 20 years old.
It was also the Yankees' first grand ​slam of the season.
Garcia opened the scoring with a 413-foot homer off Sugano to lead ‌off ⁠the second, and had his 10th multi-hit game since being acquired from Washington at the trade deadline. The first baseman also started an inning-ending double play in the fifth, when the Rockies had three hits.
In his second game back ​from a fractured rib, ​Judge had a ⁠pair of singles and played eight innings in right field.
New York starter Will Warren (10-6) allowed one run on four ​hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out eight and ​walked ⁠two.
John Schreiber, Paul Blackburn and Michael Fulmer followed with a scoreless inning of relief work apiece, allowing two combined baserunners.
Connor Norby homered and had a double for ⁠the Rockies (55-90), ​who had five hits and reached 90 ​losses for the fifth straight season.
Sugano allowed five runs on four hits in six innings. The right-hander ​struck out five, walked three and lost his fourth consecutive decision.
--Field Level Media
